results.title: Introduction - Relay Runner
results.content:
# Relay Runner

This site will help you setup a relay for personal or public use. Relays are servers that transmit notes and other stuff to clients on the Nostr network and may (or may not) store them as well.

## Why Run a Personal Relay?

Running a personal relay is a great way to keep your notes and other data under your control. You can use it as an archive for all of your data or maybe as a dedicated relay for a personal website.

## Why Run a Public Relay?

Running a public relay is a great way to decentralize and help the Nostr network grow. You also have the option to monetize your relay by charging clients for access.

## What You'll Learn

The guides will walk you through the process of setting up various relay implementations from scratch.

You'll learn how to: [...] You'll learn how to:

- Get a server
- Get a domain name
- Set up remote access using SSH
- Set up a firewall
- Set up intrusion detection
- Configure Nginx
- Obtain and set up an SSL/TLS certificate
- Build the relay software
- Install the relay software
- Configure your relay
- Set up a systemd service for your relay
- Test your relay
- Upgrade your relay

## Delayed parcels are a direct result of poverty pay for drivers

If you are wondering why your Relay parcel is delayed, missing, or sitting untouched for days, look no further than how they treat their couriers.  
Relay is shockingly stingy with the rates they offer drivers. Once you factor in fuel, courier insurance, and vehicle wear and tear, their payouts work out to well below minimum wage. Because the pay is so dire, drivers simply refuse to pick up routes unless they are completely desperate.  
You cannot expect a reliable delivery network when you exploit the people doing the actual work. Customers end up paying the price with constant delays and terrible service, all because Relay refuses to pay their couriers a fair, living rate. Pay peanuts, get delays.

## ZERO STARS [...] ## Marked as delivered to a building that…

Marked as delivered to a building that wasn’t mine.  
Relay marked my Temu parcel as delivered, but I never received it. The delivery photo showed what looked like a control room with a laptop. There’s no room like that anywhere in my block of flats.  
I couldn’t find a customer service number for Relay, and I ended up going back and forth between Relay and Temu just to get the issue dealt with. Temu is now preparing a replacement, but I’m left waiting all over again.  
Really poor delivery experience. A photo of an unfamiliar room tells me nothing about where my parcel actually went, and it shouldn’t take this much chasing to get help.

Worse courier service ever! Parcel dropped off on 12th Nov by sender, driver collected on 15th Nov, due to be delivered on 18th and still nothing. Customer service not responding. Do not use Relay as you won't get it. Lost or stolen?? Who will pay for it? Complete joke!
